records.supported_name_scope: Conecuh River is supported along the principal Alabama valley and Escambia River along the Florida receiving course. The initial modeled Old Town Creek approach and the cross-town connector at Union Springs are held separately.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selection begins east of Union Springs along the mapped Old Town Creek corridor, then makes a southward connection through Union Springs to the Conecuh headwater. Readable topography depicts Old Town Creek continuing toward the northern drainage and does not establish that southward connection across the ridge. Farther downstream, the selection follows the Conecuh southwest past Troy and Brantley through the Gantt/Andalusia impoundment setting, then west toward Brewton and south along the Escambia into Escambia Bay. Little Conecuh, Patsaliga, Sepulga, Murder Creek and Big Escambia Creek are distinct mapped arrivals, not interchangeable whole-path names. The neighboring Blackwater and Yellow systems are excluded.
records.region: Southeastern Alabama and northwestern Florida, United States: Union Springs through the Conecuh valley and Escambia delta to Escambia Bay.
records.candidate_name_role: Named lower receiving river and separately named upstream components; not a supported name for the entire selected modeled connection.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded review of both selected fragments against readable official cartography, with detailed coverage of the initial Union Springs setting and the Escambia Bay endpoint. The hold reflects positive evidence of an unsupported modeled cross-ridge connection, not absent source coverage or merely a separately named upper tributary. The downstream receiving identity is clear; continuity and naming scope across the initial connection are not established. No geometry correction or current hydraulic assessment is made.

naming_scope_details.headward_component: Old Town Creek setting east of Union Springs; the modeled connection south into Conecuh is not established.
naming_scope_details.basis_of_hold: A distinct northern drainage and unsupported cross-ridge connector are incorporated into the selected headward route. The hold is not due merely to Conecuh/Escambia naming variation or reservoirs.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: Modeled length is not an official river length. Generalization simplifies reservoirs, bends, tributary junctions and delta channels. No present flow, artificial interbasin transfer, corrected geometry, Korean label or exact name-transition point is inferred.

records.supported_name_scope: Tandileofú–Chelforó approach, Canal 2 drainage context, and an unresolved modeled lagoon/marsh continuation to Bahía de Samborombón; whole-group scalar name held.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected upstream course is in the Tandileofú–Chelforó drainage east of Tandil, passing Ayacucho and the Labardén approach. It is distinct from the more northerly Langueyú–Canal 1 drainage and the southerly Las Chilcas/Chico–Canal 5 drainage to Mar Chiquita. East of Maipú the modeled line makes a substantial lagoon/wetland detour south of the mapped Canal 2 corridor, then turns north through the General Lavalle lowlands. Its coastal endpoint lies west of the mapped Río de Ajó. Regional descriptions of Tandileofú/Chelforó discharging through Canal 2 into Ría de Ajó therefore cannot be extended to every selected reach. The observed whole route is not supported as one continuous natural river, nor as the complete mapped Canal 2 or Río de Ajó.
records.region: Buenos Aires Province, Argentina; eastern Tandilia through Ayacucho and the Maipú lowlands to the southern Samborombón coast west of General Lavalle.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded full-route correspondence and naming-scope review of both selected mainstem fragments. Readable IGN 1:250,000 cartography covers the complete generalized extent; additional 1:100,000 pixels cover the final lowland/coastal interval, with provincial atlas and report maps supplying named drainage context. The hold concerns substantial model-to-channel and natural-stream/canal/wetland scope distinctions, not missing map coverage or a minor unnamed feeder. No further source acquisition is pending now. Any future whole-group name or geometry-scope decision remains separate and unapplied; exact hydraulic connectivity and current through-flow are not established.

naming_scope_details.basis_of_hold: Substantial lagoon/marsh routing and a coastal continuation distinct from the named receiving river, together with the real natural-stream/canal composition. The hold is not caused merely by multiple upstream names.
naming_scope_details.unresolved: Whether every modeled lowland connector is hydraulically continuous, which mapped channel or diffuse drainage each follows, and what naming scope would legitimately include the final western coastal continuation.
excluded_inferences: Do not extend Tandileofú or Chelforó over the full selected length.
Do not assign Canal 2 to the lagoon detour or northbound marsh extension.
Do not call the modeled coastal segment Río de Ajó merely because the regional drainage basin uses that name.
Do not infer current discharge directions, controlled-channel operation or persistent open-water connectivity from generalized geometry.
naming_scope_details.completion_scope: Completed bounded full-route correspondence and naming-scope review of both selected mainstem fragments. Readable IGN 1:250,000 cartography covers the complete generalized extent; additional 1:100,000 pixels cover the final lowland/coastal interval, with provincial atlas and report maps supplying named drainage context. The hold concerns substantial model-to-channel and natural-stream/canal/wetland scope distinctions, not missing map coverage or a minor unnamed feeder. No further source acquisition is pending now. Any future whole-group name or geometry-scope decision remains separate and unapplied; exact hydraulic connectivity and current through-flow are not established.

records.supported_name_scope: Río Santa is printed repeatedly on the receiving valley and lower westward river. The small headward feeder is kept separate; Q. Sacsa and Q. Ancar Ragra are detailed upper-drainage map labels, not whole-selection synonyms.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The initial selection lies east of the Santa valley on the Pampa de Lampas Bajo / Pampa Cancha side, in the small eastern feeder corridor associated with the Sacsa drainage, north of Laguna Conococha. It bends southwest into the receiving Santa, then follows the long north-northwest valley through the Recuay, Huaraz, Carhuaz, Yungay and Caraz sequence, the canyon/northern bend, and the lower west-to-southwest course into the Pacific near-mouth setting north of Chimbote. It does not follow the northern Tablachaca system or eastern Manta, Quitaracsa and other tributary branches. Pando is the project context, not the location.
records.region: Áncash and adjoining La Libertad, Peru: upper Santa valley, Callejón de Huaylas, Cañón del Pato and the Pacific coastal mouth setting north of Chimbote.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded geographical correspondence across all three selected mainstem fragments using original official map pixels. The detailed headward sheet resolves the actual eastern feeder setting and excludes the standard Conococha/Tuco route; the basin sheet covers the continuous receiving Santa valley, northern bend and coast. No substantial unviewed corridor remains. Fine allocation of the first generalized cells to individual short feeder branches or exact name-transition points is not claimed and does not prevent the representative receiving identity.

naming_scope_details.upper_component: Small eastern feeder in the Sacsa-side drainage north of Conococha; detailed sheet labels Q. Sacsa and Q. Ancar Ragra separately. Exact short-fork attribution is intentionally narrower than a river-wide name assignment.
naming_scope_details.middle_component: Receiving Río Santa through Callejón de Huaylas, Cañón del Pato and the northern westward turn.
naming_scope_details.terminal_component: Lower Río Santa in the Pacific near-mouth setting north of Chimbote.
naming_scope_details.lake_passage: No selected Conococha or Aguashcocha passage; those lakes belong to nearby conventional headwater descriptions and must not be inserted into the selected path.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: Displayed modeled-path length is not an official river measurement. Generalized geometry simplifies small feeder junctions, bends and coastal channels. No new geometry, formal source or mouth, present-day hydrological condition, exact name-boundary vertex or Korean label is established.

records.supported_name_scope: Federal cartography repeatedly labels Maguse River on the eastern outlet of Imikula Lake, the intervening upper river, the approaches to and exit from Heninga Lake, the western Maguse Lake approach, and the lower Maguse Lake-to-coast river. These direct channel labels, together with continuous readable route coverage, support the representative identity. No separate river name is established for the initial western feeder.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The actual western beginning approaches the northern Carnecksluck Lake setting from the northwest, then turns east through small connecting waterbodies and northeast into the southwestern part of Imikula Lake. It does not substitute a longer northern Imikula tributary or the southern Nowyak/North Henik lake country. East of Imikula the line follows the labeled Maguse River around its southeastern and northeastern bends, passes north of Padlei, traverses northern Heninga Lake, and enters the western arms of Maguse Lake. It then turns southeast along Maguse Lake and east along the labeled lower river to the Hudson Bay coast north of Austin Island and Maguse Point. The map also shows a separate Maguse River locality farther south on the coast; that settlement-style label is not the selected endpoint. Kogtok River approaches from the north, Noomut River and Yandle Lake lie south of the middle route, and the Wallace River coastal drainage lies north of the selected lower route.
records.region: Kivalliq Region, Nunavut, Canada; western Hudson Bay hinterland through Imikula, Heninga and Maguse lakes to the coast north of Maguse Point.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded correspondence for the sole selected mainstem fragment using four newly acquired and visually inspected federal map views and retained original service metadata. The western initial feeder, named through-lakes, intermediate river bends, lower receiving channel and actual terminal coast all have readable coverage. No substantial selected route interval lacks correspondence. Unnamed small connectors, precise through-lake centerlines and exact shoreline vertices are outside this representative-system determination. An optional oversized fisheries PDF was not acquired and leaves no coverage gap.

naming_scope_details.selected_mainstem_sequence: Unnamed northwestern feeder → northern Carnecksluck Lake and small connecting waterbodies → southwestern Imikula Lake → upper Maguse River → northern Heninga Lake → Maguse River → western arms and southeastern axis of Maguse Lake → lower Maguse River → Hudson Bay coast north of Austin Island and Maguse Point.
naming_scope_details.through_lake_scope: Carnecksluck, Imikula, Heninga and Maguse are mapped lake identities on the selected corridor. Their interiors are not renamed Maguse River. Other small waterbodies are left unnamed. The finding does not determine an official river-versus-lake boundary for each generalized segment.
naming_scope_details.initial_feeder_scope: The selection begins northwest of Carnecksluck Lake, west of Imikula. No separate feeder name or official source is established; its relation to the receiving system is supported by the visible connecting watercourse and lake corridor.
naming_scope_details.tributary_scope: There are no separately selected tributary fragments. Kogtok River and nearby tributaries remain geographic context only.
naming_scope_details.nearby_unselected_waterbodies: Nowyak and North Henik lakes to the south of the western beginning, Yandle Lake and Noomut River south of the middle route, Carr Lake to the north, adjacent Tootyak Lake, and Wallace River north of the lower selected route distinguish nearby alternatives.
naming_scope_details.name_evidence_limit: The river name comes directly from readable NRCan map labels at multiple separated named channel reaches. All four map views are one cartographic publication, not independent sources. No CGN/gazetteer record, formal naming date, historical alias chain or Korean spelling is established.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The 317.307 km value is the modeled display length for this inventory selection, not an official Maguse River length. The single fragment and its stage do not establish a uniform formal river name, present flow, exact channel geometry, a lake shoreline or a naming boundary.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Keep the saved order unchanged and use later result IDs/status changes to mark progress. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated; no lake research until all river continental phases have had their review pass.
